about: Engine and live conformance cases for the HTML cache (Markdown alternate).
This file is module-only. Policy verdicts are proven by the optimizer's shared
policy cases, which this file never repeats; rows here assert what the engine
passes to the library and does with its verdicts (engine) and what each server
port sends (live). Adapter and engine changes add rows here.
ROWS. Each row has: id (unique, [a-z0-9-]), runners (one or both of engine,
live; never policy), why (a public label: an RFC section or a short rule
name), optional ports (subset of apache, nginx, iis; absent = all), and one
body per runner it names. A row whose knob a port reads differently is written
once per port with its own ports list, never as a verdict override.
engine body: config (overrides of mode, agent_optimize, max_bytes,
host_names, budget_bytes, sites), library (overrides of minor, set_bound,
html_mode, agent_entitled for the fake library), volume (entries present
before the first step: kind original | sidecar | markdown | withheld | epoch),
verdicts (results the fake library returns, consumed in order per fn; a
store verdict may carry the reason detail, such as request for a request
no-store), and
steps. A step has kind (capture | serve | poll_tick | stats_tick |
admin_purge), optional pre (ops run before it), request, response (capture:
status, origin, store_delta, final_delta, module, body_ref, aborted), during
(capture only: [{point before_send | after_send | after_commit |
after_recheck, do: [ops]}]; before_send is after capture_start and before the
origin request goes out)
and expect. pre and do ops are one-key objects: purge_url, purge_global,
flush_file, wipe_file_cache, create_engine, advance_clock, make_visible,
disable_recheck, budget. expect keys: calls (an ordered subsequence of the
library calls made in the step: other calls may come between, and each
listed call is matched on the subset of arguments given; dotted names
address struct fields; a call's exact [request | stored] makes the match
fail when the call carried a field of that struct the args do not name, so
the row states the whole struct: every flag bit, flags_unknown for any bit
without a name, and a hash as zero or sha256:<body>), calls_exclude (fns
never called in the step),
port_calls and port_calls_exclude (port methods called or never called),
stored, removed,
notify ([] = none), counters (deltas), serve {kind fall_through | final,
status, reason, headers_exact (the complete header set the port is asked to
emit: no other line), body_bytes}, log_lines, admin_response,
purge_set_added, volume_epoch_s, budget_in_use. An absent key is not
asserted. A volume original with paired true has a stamp equal to the
pairing hash of the volume's sidecar entry for the same url; with no sidecar
entry it needs no header block. A header value $len:<body> is the byte
length of that entry of bodies.
live body: mode, agent_optimize, vhost (knobs: header_add, header_always,
header_early, expires, auth, alias, default_vhost, in_place,
pagespeed_off_location, compress_markdown, third_party_filter, merge_slashes,
poll_interval_s, chained_module_origin), origin {status, headers, body_ref,
echo_conditionals}, and steps [{request {method, path, host, headers}, pre,
process, background, expect}]. live pre ops: purge_url {url, form PURGE |
query}, purge_global {via admin | flush_file}, wait_markdown {timeout_s,
expect_ready (default true; false = the copy must NOT become servable
within the timeout)}, sleep_s,
origin_set, hold_origin, release_origin, set_mode. live expect keys: status,
content_type, headers_exact (name -> {count, value | contains}),
headers_only (no header beyond headers_exact and the server core's
transport lines Date, Server, Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding),
headers_absent, stored (an original entry for the request URL is present
in the volume after the step, read by exact id), stored_lifetime_s,
sidecar_absent, body_ref,
body_bytes, length_matches_body, origin_saw, origin_saw_absent,
counter_delta, differential {against: modes, allow_vary_accept}. The request
header value $markdown_etag is replaced by the ETag of the last Markdown 200.
